content:
After months of beta testing, Apple today officially launched Siri AI to the public as part of the iOS 27 and other operating system updates.

During setup, users will see a new prompt asking them whether they want to opt in to help improve Siri and Apple Intelligence. Here's what this option means.

Prior to today, users were asked during setup whether they wanted to help improve Siri and Dictation. If they opted in, Siri and Dictation's audio and text transcripts would be shared with Apple.

Starting today, when users enable Siri AI, they will see a setup screen asking whether they want to opt in to "Improve Siri and Apple Intelligence," with two options: "Share Audio and Text" or "Not Now."

Apple explains:

Improve Siri & Apple Intelligence – Help improve foundation models and Siri by allowing Apple to collect and use text and audio interactions from you with Siri, Dictation, and Translate.

It's worth noting here that if you opt in to this setting, there's actually no change in the type of data Apple collects. What's changed is that Apple will now use this data to train and improve its foundation models, as well as Siri and Dictation as always.

Even users who previously opted in under the older setting will be asked again when they enable Siri AI. This gives them a chance to re-evaluate their choice, as the data will now also be used to train Apple foundation models.

Apple has made clear its privacy safeguards when asking users whether to opt in. The company said that Siri audio data, text transcripts, and related data will be tied to a "randomly generated device identifier that rotates frequently, multiple times per hour" and will not be linked to your Apple Account or email address. Apple also does not use this data to build marketing profiles, nor will it sell it to anyone.

You can turn this option on or off at any time by going to Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements > Improve Siri & Apple Intelligence.

Apple has also published a new support document detailing how these settings apply across all platforms.
